pairs.why: B uses a raised camera showing the rover's top face over a plane that recedes, like the real high 3/4 cards, while A is low and front-on with a dome-like ground.
B turns the target disc so its thickness shows and shows more of the shelf top, like the real card, while A's target is nearly flat-on.
Both view the fins from a similar high angle, but B's perspective is milder and the fins are less flared toward the viewer, as on the real card.
B shows a tilted 3/4 view with the body's side thickness visible like the real calculator, while A is almost a flat top-down plate.
B's camera is higher, so the top faces and the floor plane read like the real card, while A is low with stronger perspective and a tall side view.
A's glass fills the frame with a similar rim ellipse and table-wall horizon as the real card, while B's small glass leaves a lot of empty depth, but the difference is slight.
Both drawings are frontal and symmetric, while the real kit is turned in 3/4 view, so neither matches the camera.
A's horizon height and open planter ellipse sit slightly nearer the real card's camera, but the two are almost the same.
